items.title: Russia's war on Ukraine: 'Americans want to have a deal whatever the cost for both Ukraine & Europe'
items.summary: Delano D'Souza is pleased to welcome Grégoire Roos, Director of the Europe and Russia and Eurasia Programmes at Chatham House. As European countries prepare to take part in the next round of Ukraine peace talks, Roos questions whether having five European representatives could weaken their negotiating position. "The other option is to realize that it dilutes the negotiating power of Europe. And I would lean towards that," he says, proposing Finnish President Alexander Stubb as a possible representative. Roos also points to differences between Washington and European governments over negotiations with Russia. While "the Americans do absolutely want to have a deal whatever the cost for both Ukraine and Europe," he argues that European governments have little choice but to maintain pressure on Moscow, which has yet to abandon its "maximalist demands."

Colpito pure il ponte di Crimea. Sospeso il traffico lungo l'unico collegamento via terra (sia stradale che ferroviario) tra la Russia continentale e la penisola di annessa da Mosca nel 2014.  Poche ore prima della (nuova) offensiva ucraina ben oltre il classico fronte di guerra, Zelensky rivendicava: “Abbiamo messo fuori uso il 55 per cento della capacità di raffinazione russa”. Nel frattempo Mosca 'gela' del cancellerie del Vecchio Continente. L’avvertimento del portavoce del Cremlino Dmitry Peskov ("o intesa con l’Europa o procederemo con la forza”) alza il livello di tensione nei negoziati proprio nelle ore in cui gli Stati Uniti intensificano il pressing diplomatico per far sedere anche gli europei al tavolo delle trattative i nsieme all’Ucraina e alla Russia.   Provocazioni russe che accompagnano gli atti di sabotaggio verso i paesi eu

items.title: European Day in Remembrance of the Victims of Accidents at Work: Statement by President Meloni
items.summary: Following its formal adoption by the Council of the European Union, 8 August has today become the ‘European Day in Remembrance of the Victims of Accidents at Work and for the Protection and Dignity of Workers’. This date is the anniversary of the 1956 tragedy in Marcinelle, where 262 miners of various nationalities died, 136 of them Italian. Thanks to the late Minister Tremaglia, on this day for the last 25 years, Italy has commemorated the sacrifice made by Italian workers around the world. As of today, this remembrance belongs to all Europeans, thanks to an Italian initiative which was endorsed by a large majority of the European Parliament and which this Government has firmly supported. A day to strongly reaffirm that work must always be synonymous with dignity, rights and safety, and that there can be no room in Europe for those who exploit and enslave people, fuelling illegal human trafficking to obtain low-cost labour and to roll back workers’ rights. items.title: Relocation of Cape Town baboons to sanctuary ignites heated protests

The 44-member Waterfall troop (named after the area they mainly inhabit) was captured in the southern seaside suburb of Simon’s Town on Friday and Saturday.
